name: contaminated_reads_chimeric_assembly
mechanism: A Salmonella Typhimurium read set is spiked with 20% E. coli K-12 reads before assembly. The two organisms are both Enterobacteriaceae (~98% ANI at housekeeping genes) and share conserved sequences including 16S rRNA, core metabolic genes, and IS elements. Their shared k-mers act as bridges in the de Bruijn graph, connecting otherwise distinct subgraphs. The assembler produces chimeric contigs at these bridge points — sequences that begin in Typhimurium genomic context and end in E. coli context. No assembler emits a contamination warning. The output FASTA passes basic QC metrics (N50, total length) and appears to be a reasonable 5-6 Mb assembly. Downstream typing tools (SeqSero2, mlst) receive chimeric sequences containing partial Salmonella antigen genes joined to E. coli flanking sequence.

known_behaviors.behavior: Assembles both organisms simultaneously. Shared k-mer regions (16S, housekeeping genes, IS elements) act as graph bridges. Produces chimeric contigs of plausible length. Total assembled length ~7-8 Mb (inflated beyond either genome alone). Exit 0, no contamination warning.
More conservative overlap handling reduces chimera frequency but does not eliminate it. May discard some low-coverage E. coli contigs as noise, masking the contamination rather than flagging it.

samples.description: Salmonella Typhimurium PNUSAS576962 reads — the 'true' organism (80% of final read pool)

download.command: fasterq-dump --gzip --outdir . SRR38945246 && mv SRR38945246_1.fastq.gz reads_1.fq.gz && mv SRR38945246_2.fastq.gz reads_2.fq.gz

samples.description: E. coli K-12 MG1655 reads — the contaminant (downsampled to 20% of Typhimurium read count)

download.command: fasterq-dump --gzip --outdir . SRR1770413 && mv SRR1770413_1.fastq.gz reads_1.fq.gz && mv SRR1770413_2.fastq.gz reads_2.fq.gz

samples.description: Final mixed read set: 100% Typhimurium reads + 20% E. coli reads concatenated — the input to the assembler

recipe.description: Subsample E. coli reads to ~20% of Typhimurium read count (seed 42), then concatenate with Typhimurium reads. SRR38945246 has ~984k spots; 20% = ~197k E. coli spots.
recipe.command: seqtk sample -s42 ../ecoli_contaminant/reads_1.fq.gz 196880 | gzip > ecoli_sub_1.fq.gz && seqtk sample -s42 ../ecoli_contaminant/reads_2.fq.gz 196880 | gzip > ecoli_sub_2.fq.gz && cat ../typhimurium_reads/reads_1.fq.gz ecoli_sub_1.fq.gz > reads_1.fq.gz && cat ../typhimurium_reads/reads_2.fq.gz ecoli_sub_2.fq.gz > reads_2.fq.gz && rm ecoli_sub_1.fq.gz ecoli_sub_2.fq.gz

download.command: echo 'mixed_reads is recipe-based; run acquire.py to generate from typhimurium_reads and ecoli_contaminant'

curation.notes: 20% contamination fraction is chosen to exceed typical contamination detection thresholds while remaining plausible as a lab cross-contamination event. At 20%, the E. coli coverage is ~10-12x — above the k-mer frequency threshold that SPAdes would discard as sequencing error, so the contaminant actively participates in graph construction.
